children: CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV, Financials), an AI cloud provider, is becoming a test case of how far investors would go to fund the AI boom.
The company's bonds, issued in June at a yield of 9.675%, have plummeted so much that yields are up to around 15%. That's more important than another terrible day for the stock.
Credit investors are asking if the cash future data-centre projects will earn will arrive fast enough to support the debt incurred today.
The argument is about CoreWeave, which depends significantly on external financing to finance its expansion.
Investors are also beginning to look closely at leverage, collateral and the chance that pricey GPUs might become obsolete before certain facilities are up and running.
The wider conclusion is that it could be tougher and more expensive to support AI infrastructure.
Dan Ives puts the figure of planned projects that may never be constructed at 5% to 10%.
That doesn't imply the AI buildout is done, though. It does indicate capital is getting less forgiving.
The next thing to monitor is whether CoreWeave bond yields stabilize, since sustained stress might change the price and availability of loans throughout the larger AI infrastructure market.

title: CoreWeave Bond Rout Raises New Questions About AI Infrastructure Spending
